description: HEY, WE ARE ASTRA We are tackling the challenge to build a health monitoring software for astronauts on long-duration space missions. Our goal is to create an intuitive and robust tool that gathers vital health indicators,  to autonomously evaluate and act on their physical and behavioral well-being in a hostile closed environment.
summary: A dashboard was developed that can connect to existing devices in suits and spacecraft (such as the Bio-monitor, ARCHeR, etc.), integrating them into a unified environment. This system features an interface and an assistant designed to improve accessibility, with a particular focus on the crew's psychological well-being. It serves as a constant companion throughout the mission—helping to mitigate feelings of isolation—and functions as a health assistant (monitoring heart rate, blood and muscle oxygenation, muscle mass density, and levels of ROS and RNS). It also includes data tracking (for sleep schedules and stress levels), alert notifications, and a dedicated space for relaxation.
details:
What It Does & How It Works

Our project is an intelligent, centralized dashboard designed to unify existing devices, sensors, and telemetry systems within spacesuits into a single high-accessibility digital ecosystem. Instead of forcing astronauts to monitor fragmented displays, the platform translates complex, scattered data into intuitive visual information powered by an interactive virtual assistant.

The system operates through three integrated modules:

Data Control and Alert Center: Monitors vital systems in real time and delivers predictive anomaly alerts.

Holistic Health Assistant: Continuously tracks physical biomarkers (heart rate, HRV, SpO2, body temperature, oxidative stress, and muscle mass) alongside psychological well-being.

Relaxation Space: Provides an immersive environment for mental rest and emotional regulation during downtime.

To function without restricted astronaut medical records, the analytics engine uses generative AI synthetic data trained on aerospace medical literature to build a nominal physiological baseline. Incoming sensor streams are continuously compared against this baseline; if statistical deviations occur (such as sustained tachycardia paired with high cognitive load), the system automatically triggers preventive alerts or recommends relaxation interventions.

Benefits & Intended Impact

Eliminating Cognitive Overload & Alarm Fatigue: By consolidating telemetry into one intuitive interface, astronauts process critical data faster under high-pressure conditions and avoid mental burnout.

Cost-Effective Interoperability: The software-first architecture leverages sensors already integrated into current spacesuits, avoiding expensive physical hardware redesigns while remaining hardware-agnostic and scalable for live deployment.

Safeguarding Long-Duration Missions: On deep-space voyages to the Moon or Mars where communication delays with Earth and extreme isolation pose severe risks the platform transforms spacesuit instrumentation from a cold control panel into an active, human-centric ally that protects physical health, preserves crew cohesion, and prevents human error.

Tools, Hardware, Software & Technologies Used

Hardware & Sensors: Arduino microcontrollers paired with AD8232 ECG heart-rate sensors, alongside prototypes integrating RONSS (reactive oxygen, nitrogen, and sulfur species) oxidative stress sensors, near-infrared spectroscopy (NIRS) tissue oxygenation concepts, and EMG/EIM muscle mass tracking.

3D Modeling & Visualization: Blender (v3.6.23) and three.js (r160) utilizing glTF 2.0 (.glb) models adapted from the open-source Z-Anatomy and BodyParts3D anatomical databases.

AI & Interface Design: Generative AI algorithms for synthetic biometric baseline modeling, real-time statistical anomaly detection, signal filtering/smoothing pipelines, and Space Grotesk typography for high-accessibility UI/UX design.

Creativity & Key Factors Considered

Creative Innovation: Rather than treating astronaut health and suit telemetry as separate engineering problems, we merged clinical biomedical monitoring, 3D anatomical visualization, and mental health decompression into a single companion ecosystem using synthetic AI modeling to solve the real-world barrier of space medical data privacy.

Data Privacy & Scarcity: Overcoming restricted access to real astronaut physiological histories through scientifically grounded synthetic baselines.

Signal Integrity: Addressing real-world electrical noise, motion artifacts, and signal clipping (such as false ST-elevation warnings) during hardware prototyping to ensure clean, reliable real-time readings.

Spaceflight Stressors: Accounting for microgravity muscle degradation, ionizing cosmic radiation (oxidative stress), hypoxia/decompression risks, and the psychological toll of prolonged confinement.
